title: Compose CLI: Up, Down, Logs & More 🎮
description: Master the essential Compose commands to control your entire application stack.

slides.title: Starting the Application: `up` 🚀
slides.content:
# `docker compose up`

Builds, (re)creates, and starts containers.

Common options:
- `-d` – detached mode (background)
- `--build` – rebuild images before starting
- `--force-recreate` – recreate containers even if configuration hasn’t changed
- `--no-deps` – don’t start linked services

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Starts the whole stack. If images need building, it builds them first.

slides.title: Stopping and Cleaning: `down` 🧹
slides.content:
# `docker compose down`

Stops containers and removes containers, networks created by `up`.

Add `-v` to also remove volumes (caution!):
```bash
docker compose down -v
```

Add `--rmi` to remove images:
```bash
docker compose down --rmi all
```

> Use `docker compose stop` to just stop without removing resources.

quizData.question: What does `docker compose up` do that `docker compose start` does not?

options.text: Creates containers and networks if they don't exist

quizData.explanation: `start` only starts existing stopped containers. `up` creates them if needed, and also creates networks/volumes.

slides.title: Viewing Logs and Status 📋
slides.content:
# `docker compose logs` & `docker compose ps`

See logs from all or specific services:
```bash
docker compose logs -f
```
- `-f` follows output
- `--tail 50` last 50 lines
- add service name to filter: `docker compose logs web`

Check running containers:
```bash
docker compose ps
```

> These commands work only when run from the directory containing `compose.yaml` (or specify with `-f`).

quizData.question: Which command shows the status of only the services defined in your current compose file?
quizData.explanation: `docker compose ps` lists containers that belong to the current project.

slides.title: Running One‑Off Commands: `exec` & `run` ⚡
slides.content:
# Interact with Services

- `docker compose exec <service> <command>` – run a command in a running service container (like `docker exec`).
- `docker compose run <service> <command>` – start a new container for the service, overriding the command.

**Example:**
```bash
docker compose exec web bash
docker compose run --rm web python manage.py migrate
```

`run` respects volumes, networks, and dependencies (unless `--no-deps`).

slides.title: Other Useful Commands 🧰
slides.content:
# Compose Toolkit

- `docker compose restart` – restart services.
- `docker compose pull` – pull latest images.
- `docker compose build` – build or rebuild services.
- `docker compose config` – validate and view the merged compose file.
- `docker compose top` – display running processes.
- `docker compose pause/unpause` – freeze/unfreeze containers.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Graceful Shutdown
`docker compose down -t 20` gives containers 20 seconds to gracefully stop before killing them (default is 10s).
